classification_rules: Every recorded affiliation must be stated in a source that itself ties the claim to the SIPRI monograph authorship (publisher bio, journal contributor note, or library authority record for the book).
No modern 'Chris Smith' listing was accepted without a monograph-anchored bridge; homonymous politicians, musicians, and academics were excluded.
Current status of the 1994 roles is unresolved and promoted to an investigation target rather than asserted.

findings.result: SIPRI publicly lists Chris Smith as author of India's Ad Hoc Arsenal: Direction or Drift in Defence Policy? (OUP/SIPRI 1994) on its bio and publication pages.

The OUP author bio publicly lists him as Senior Research Fellow at the Centre for Defence Studies, King's College London and Director of the Centre's North-South Defence and Security Programme (as published 1994); the 2001 Conflict, Security & Development contributor note corroborates the same author profile.
Library authority record for the monograph gives the authorized name 'Smith, Chris (Chris Nicholas), 1955-', recorded on the person document for future disambiguation.
No current-day organizational listing of this individual was corroborated in this pass; unresolved target created.

data.method: Repository search; SIPRI bio and 1994 publication page review; Brave web discovery of publisher author bios and journal contributor notes; strict disambiguation anchoring every claim to the monograph; canonical batch import; Nim merge gate.
data.research_question: Which dark-academia component organizations, companies, government bodies, boards, and advisory groups publicly list Chris Smith?
